subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: What framework-level plugin circuit breaker contract should OpenClaw support for plugin hooks/tools, persisted state, operator controls, and default degradation behavior?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but choosing fail modes, forced-open behavior, status/reset surfaces, storage schema, SDK/API exposure, and default-on policy changes third-party plugin and gateway runtime contracts.

options.title: Design core breaker contract first
options.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, metrics/status/reset surfaces, compatibility defaults, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep breakers plugin-owned
options.body: Continue with plugin-local breakers like Active Memory and add only narrow SDK helpers if repeated plugin needs prove a shared seam is required.

options.title: Telemetry-first rollout
options.body: Add attribution and passive log-only evaluation first, then decide active open/half-open behavior after real deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker contract first
recommendation.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, metrics/status/reset surfaces, compatibility defaults, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history across hook timeout, plugin tool, and session-lock reliability code touched by the design.
